    - Some of the dusk routes fly again, *Player*. Not all. On a few roads east the birds still turn back at dusk, and I still write them down. But the list is shorter than it was. I never thought I would see it shrink.
    - The routes over the Highbeacon are open. Greyfeather's daughter flew one at noon yesterday, and again at dusk. I watched her the whole way.
    - Stormcrest sleeps at noon on the Highbeacon. Whenever you are ready, I will tell you the wind.
    - My list, *Player*. You are on it now, in a way. In the margin, beside the route you walked.
    - The loft is quiet just now. Sit, if you like. What would you like to know?
        - *Choice:* Tell me about the pigeons.
        - *Choice:* Which routes do the birds refuse?
        - *Choice:* Why is there a cat in a pigeon loft?
        - *Choice:* To the Highbeacon.

    - The birds carry messages to the other towns; the runners carry them inside the city. I learned the loft from Isolde Spurr, who kept it before me, and I have kept it since I was twenty. Fifty-one years on the Crooked Tower.
    - I understand birds better than people. I admit it freely. Birds never ask me what I meant.
    - It began a few years ago with old Greyfeather, who would not take the road east at dusk. Then others would not. Some routes are refused only at dusk. A few at any hour. I keep a careful list.
    - The all-hours routes fly again, since Stormcrest. The dusk ones are different. Some have opened, some have not, and the birds will not tell me why. I keep the list as carefully as ever.
    - Starling brings up the flicker dates and we lay them side by side. Some match. Some do not. Neither of us knows what that means. We drink the tea anyway.
    - Pounce arrived one wet autumn, years ago, and decided the loft was his. The pigeons have accepted him with deep reluctance. He sleeps beside the little iron cat Ferro made for us last Walkout Day. I think he believes it is his sister.
    - The wind is from the west today; it will push you toward the tower's edge, so keep your back to the beacon cup. Go at noon, *Player*, while it sleeps. And come back.
    - Mind the stair on the way down. The birds will see you off.
